ru: не было бы счастья, да несчастье помогло
definition: Something that seems bad initially but ultimately has a positive result.
examples: Losing that job turned out to be a blessing in disguise.

ru: зануда, тот, кто портит всем настроение; облом
definition: Someone or something that spoils other people's enjoyment or excitement.
examples: Don't be a buzzkill — we're just celebrating.

term: a hell of a lot (of something)
ru: чертовски много, до хрена, гораздо (перед сравнительной степенью)
definition: An extremely large amount or quantity of something.
examples: We spent a hell of a lot of time fixing the problem.

ru: линия взгляда / прямая видимость, поле зрения
definition: A clear, unobstructed path between an observer and what they can see.
examples: The trees blocked our line of sight to the entrance.

ru: ощущение смысла, чувство цели (понимание, ради чего ты что-то делаешь)
definition: The feeling that your actions have meaning and a clear goal.
examples: Volunteering gave her a renewed sense of purpose.

definition: During the days at the end of the working week, either generally or on a particular occasion.
examples: I usually go hiking at weekends.
note: Common in British English; American usage often on weekends / on the weekend.

ru: если бы не; если бы не кто-то / что-то; без (кого-то / чего-то)
definition: If it had not been for a particular person or thing.
examples: But for your help, we would have missed the deadline.

term: in for a penny, in for a pound
ipa: /ˌɪn fər ə ˈpeni ˌɪn fər ə ˈpaʊnd/
ru: сказал «а» — говори «б»; взялся за гуж — не говори, что не дюж; гулять так гулять
definition: Once committed to something, you should see it through even if it becomes difficult.
examples: We've started the renovation; in for a penny, in for a pound.

definition: Briefly or casually, without giving something much attention.
examples: She mentioned the vacancy in passing.

definition: In the part of a picture or scene closest to the viewer.
examples: A cyclist appears in the foreground of the photograph.

term: on the decline / on the wane
definition: Becoming less common, strong, popular or successful.
examples: Demand for the product is on the decline.

definition: People in general rather than the wealthy, famous or powerful.
examples: The policy will affect ordinary people most.

definition: So costly that paying for it is practically impossible or unreasonable.
examples: Housing in the city centre is prohibitively expensive.

definition: Slightly fat, especially with a soft, rounded appearance.
examples: The puppy had a pudgy little belly.

definition: The part of a seat that supports a person's back.
examples: He hung his jacket over the back of a chair.

ru: привлекать, нравиться кому-то. That's what appeals to me most — именно это мне больше всего нравится.
definition: To attract or interest a person; to seem enjoyable or desirable to them.
examples: The chance to work independently really appeals to me.

ru: это надолго, пришло всерьёз и навсегда
definition: To have become a lasting part of life rather than a temporary trend.
examples: Remote work looks as though it's here to stay.

term: to blur the line(s) between X and Y
ru: стирать / размывать грань между X и Y
definition: To make the distinction between two things less clear.
examples: AI can blur the line between human and machine-generated content.

term: to come as a surprise (to someone)
definition: To be unexpected or cause someone to feel surprised.
examples: The decision came as a surprise to everyone.

term: to get the hang of something
definition: To learn how to do something through practice and become comfortable with it.
examples: I'm finally getting the hang of the new software.

term: to play a role in something
definition: To have an influence or function in a process or situation.
examples: Trust plays a crucial role in negotiations.

term: to pose a risk to something / someone
definition: To create the possibility of harm or danger for someone or something.
examples: The delay could pose a risk to patient safety.

ru: 1) основываться на, зависеть от, держаться на; 2) лежать / опираться на; (о взгляде) остановиться на
definition: To depend on or be based on a particular fact, principle or condition.
examples: The whole argument rests on a questionable assumption.

term: to show no sign(s) of slowing down
ru: не собирается замедляться, не сбавляет темп
definition: To continue at a fast rate without any indication of becoming slower.
examples: The company shows no signs of slowing down.

definition: To speak about someone or something with enthusiastic approval.
examples: Her former colleagues keep singing her praises.

definition: To tell people about a potential danger or unwanted development.
examples: Experts warned of further disruption.

term: would love it if … (I'd love it if …)
ru: Я был бы очень рад, если бы... / Мне бы очень хотелось, чтобы...
definition: To strongly wish for a particular event or situation to happen.
examples: I'd love it if we could finish early today.

definition: A continuing increase in how quickly something is growing or changing.
examples: The report found a sustained acceleration in productivity growth.

definition: The first assessment of the monetary worth of a business or asset.
examples: The initial valuation was lower than investors expected.

term: at a fraction of the cost
ru: за малую долю стоимости, в разы дешевле
definition: For a much smaller share of the usual or expected price.
examples: The software provides similar features at a fraction of the cost.

ru: в целом, взвесив все за и против; в итоге
definition: Considering all the advantages and disadvantages together.
examples: On balance, the benefits outweigh the risks.

definition: The arguments and evidence supporting a particular proposal or position.
examples: She made a convincing case for reform.

ru: подать заявку / откликнуться на вакансию, устраиваться на работу
definition: To submit an application to be considered for employment.
examples: I applied for a job at a technology company.
note: Apply for a position, but apply to a company.

ru: подать заявку в компанию, обратиться в компанию (на работу)
definition: To send an application to an organisation, especially seeking employment.
examples: She applied to several companies before getting an interview.

definition: To investigate a business or transaction carefully before a major decision.
examples: The buyer carried out due diligence before the acquisition.

ru: последовать примеру, сделать то же самое
definition: To do the same thing that another person or organisation has just done.
examples: One bank reduced its fees, and others followed suit.

term: to harness the strengths of something
definition: To make effective use of the advantages or abilities of something.
examples: The team needs to harness the strengths of both approaches.

term: to keep a firm grip on something
definition: To maintain strong control over a situation or activity.
examples: The manager kept a firm grip on spending.

term: to laud the benefits of something
definition: To praise the positive effects or advantages of something enthusiastically.
examples: Executives lauded the benefits of the new system.

term: to make significant inroads into something
ru: значительно продвинуться, заметно потеснить, проникнуть (на рынок, в сферу)
definition: To achieve substantial progress in an area or gain share in a market.
examples: The company made significant inroads into the European market.

definition: To invest large amounts of money in a project or activity.
examples: The firm is ploughing cash into research.
note: British spelling plough; American plow.

ru: вызывать серьёзные опасения; поднимать серьёзные вопросы
definition: To cause significant worry or bring important problems to public attention.
examples: The proposal raised serious concerns about privacy.

definition: To continue being responsible and answerable for something.
examples: Senior managers remain accountable for the decision.

definition: To hurry and work hard to reach the level of someone who is ahead.
examples: Smaller firms are scrambling to catch up.

definition: To make brief contact with someone to exchange updates or coordinate.
examples: Let's touch base after the meeting.
note: Informal business English; touch base with someone.

definition: A system that enables direct communication between the brain and an electronic device.
examples: Researchers developed a brain–computer interface for communication.

definition: A substantial amount of freedom to act or make decisions independently.
examples: The robot operates with a high degree of autonomy.

definition: A military underwater vessel powered by a nuclear reactor.
examples: A nuclear submarine can remain submerged for long periods.
note: Nuclear refers to propulsion, not necessarily to weapons.

definition: To put artificial-intelligence applications into practical use.
examples: The firm deployed AI tools to review contracts.

definition: To accept and actively adopt recently developed technical methods or devices.
examples: Smaller businesses are starting to embrace new technology.

definition: To make a process happen much faster to a substantial degree.
examples: Better computing power could profoundly accelerate discovery.

term: to train on vast amounts of data
definition: To develop a model using extremely large datasets as training material.
examples: The system was trained on vast amounts of data.
note: An AI model is trained on data; people train with materials.

definition: A hospital room specially equipped for surgical operations.
examples: The patient was taken to the operating theatre.

definition: A rubber-coated weight disc designed to be safely dropped during lifting.
examples: Use a bumper plate when practising Olympic lifts.

definition: To put weight plates onto a barbell before an exercise.
examples: Load the bar with another ten kilos.

definition: To increase the speed or intensity of an activity or competition.
examples: The runners pushed the pace in the final kilometre.

definition: A legal requirement to make specified information available to others.
examples: The regulations impose mandatory disclosure of certain risks.

definition: To be at risk of formal punishment at work for breaking rules.
examples: An employee may face disciplinary action for serious misconduct.

term: to prompt regulators to step in
definition: To cause government supervisors to intervene in a situation.
examples: The incident prompted regulators to step in.

definition: For a dispute or case to come before a court for consideration.
examples: The dispute eventually reached court.
note: Also common: the case went to court.

definition: To weaken people's confidence in institutions or authorities.
examples: The scandal undermined public trust in the regulator.

definition: To make courts and legal remedies more accessible to people.
examples: The reforms aim to widen access to justice.

definition: A sudden, sharp feeling of embarrassment or guilt.
examples: She felt a pang of shame when she remembered what she had said.
note: Common: to feel a pang of shame; also a pang of guilt / regret.

definition: To spend time and energy trying to achieve or improve something.
examples: She put a lot of effort into improving her English.
note: put effort into + noun / -ing.

definition: To turn out or develop in a particular way.
examples: Things did not pan out as we had hoped.

term: to be reluctant to do something
definition: To feel hesitant or unwilling to do something.
examples: He was reluctant to accept the offer.
note: be reluctant to + infinitive; it does not necessarily mean refusal.

definition: To deal with distressing psychological consequences after an event.
examples: She faced the emotional fallout of losing her job.
note: In a specific context, often: face the emotional fallout of/from something.

definition: To set aside pride to do something necessary but uncomfortable.
examples: He swallowed his pride and apologised.

definition: To change your focus or approach to something.
examples: Let’s switch gears and discuss the budget.
note: Especially common in American English; British change gear is also used.

definition: To reach an agreement with someone, usually after negotiation, with benefits or concessions for both sides.
examples: After lengthy negotiations, the two companies finally struck a bargain.
We struck a bargain: I would handle the research, and she would prepare the presentation.
note: Usually: strike a bargain with someone; strike a bargain over/on something. More formal than make a deal.

term: to come to terms with something
ru: смириться с чем-либо; принять неприятную действительность
definition: To gradually accept and learn to deal with a difficult or unpleasant situation that cannot be changed.
examples: It took him months to come to terms with losing his job.
She is still struggling to come to terms with the end of the relationship.
note: Often used with loss, failure, reality, or the fact that…; implies gradual psychological acceptance, not merely agreement.

definition: To recognise that someone is being dishonest or that something is not what it appears to be.
examples: She saw through his lies immediately.
I could see through his excuse from the start.
note: see through someone or their lies/excuses — detect pretence or dishonesty; distinct from see something through (finish it).

ru: довести что-либо до конца, несмотря на трудности
definition: To continue doing something until it is finished, despite difficulties.
examples: Despite all the setbacks, she was determined to see the project through.
We promised to see the plan through to the end.
note: Separable: see a project through / see it through; see something through to completion. Not the same as see through someone's lies.

ru: дать неприятной ситуации, конфликту или скандалу утихнуть; переждать
definition: To wait for an unpleasant situation or disagreement to become less serious or be forgotten.
examples: Let's wait a few days and let the whole thing blow over.
He decided not to respond immediately and let the controversy blow over.
note: Common: let it blow over / let the whole thing blow over. Do not confuse with let it blow (literally, allow wind to blow).

term: to take an emotional toll (on someone)
ru: эмоционально истощать; тяжело сказываться на психологическом состоянии человека
definition: To cause significant emotional stress, suffering or exhaustion over time.
examples: Working in a toxic environment can take a serious emotional toll on employees.
The prolonged uncertainty took an emotional toll on her.
note: Common: take a heavy/serious emotional toll on someone; take a toll on someone's mental health.

ru: вовремя остановиться, чтобы избежать дальнейших потерь; прекратить бесперспективное дело
definition: To stop an unsuccessful activity or leave a bad situation to avoid losing even more.
examples: I realised the job wasn't right for me, so I decided to cut my losses and leave.
After months of poor sales, the company decided to cut its losses and close the project.
note: Often used about business, investments, work and relationships. Losses may involve money, time or effort. Pronoun changes with subject: cut my/our/your/their losses.

ru: получить более привлекательную должность; добиться перехода на лучшую позицию
definition: To successfully obtain a more desirable job or position, often with better pay, responsibilities or working conditions.
examples: He left the company after securing a better role elsewhere.
She hopes to secure a better role with greater autonomy and career prospects.
note: Formal business English: secure a role/position means successfully obtain it; more formal than get a better job.

ru: квалификация; профессиональная подготовка; диплом или сертификат; требование к кандидату
definition: A skill, achievement, certificate or level of education that makes someone suitable for a particular job or activity.
examples: She has all the necessary qualifications for the position.
Legal qualifications and relevant experience are essential for this role.
note: Often plural (qualifications) for credentials and job requirements. Common: professional qualifications, academic qualifications, meet the qualifications for a job.

ru: начать сомневаться в принятом решении; передумать
definition: To begin doubting a decision that you have already made.
examples: I had second thoughts about accepting the offer.
She is having second thoughts about moving abroad.
note: Usually have second thoughts about something; not the same as thinking something through.

definition: To involve a disadvantage or sacrifice in exchange for a benefit.
examples: Career success often comes at a cost.
The extra flexibility came at a considerable cost.
note: Often used when an apparent benefit has a hidden drawback.

definition: Used in ordinary informal conversation rather than formal language.
examples: That is a colloquial expression, not a legal term.
His writing is clear but sometimes rather colloquial.
note: Adjective: colloquial language, a colloquial expression; related noun: colloquialism.

definition: The shape and overall physical appearance of a person's body.
examples: He developed an impressive physique through years of training.
Her athletic physique reflects her dedication to sport.
note: Common: muscular, athletic, lean or impressive physique.

definition: A body shape marked by visibly developed muscles.
examples: Building a muscular physique takes consistent training.
He maintained a muscular physique well into his forties.
note: Physique refers to body build, not simply strength.

definition: A prestigious international professional bodybuilding competition associated with the Mr Olympia title.
examples: Winning at the Olympia is a major achievement in professional bodybuilding.
Several elite bodybuilders competed at the Olympia.
note: Here: Olympia / Mr Olympia bodybuilding contest, not the ancient Greek site or the Olympic Games.

ru: выиграть генетическую лотерею; иметь удачные врождённые данные
definition: To be born with unusually favourable inherited traits.
examples: Some athletes seem to have won the genetic lottery.
He won the genetic lottery when it came to muscle-building potential.
note: Informal, figurative phrase; often used about appearance or athletic ability.

term: there is some truth to something
definition: A claim or opinion is partly accurate, even if it is not entirely correct.
examples: There is some truth to the criticism.
There is some truth to what you are saying, but the situation is more complex.
note: Common: there is some truth to that / to the argument; allows qualified agreement.

definition: To be significant, purposeful or understandable rather than empty or pointless.
examples: People want their work to have meaning.
The gesture had special meaning for her.
note: Can refer to purpose, personal significance or linguistic sense.

definition: To stop trying to achieve an objective that you previously intended to pursue.
examples: He refused to abandon his goal despite repeated setbacks.
Sometimes it is sensible to abandon a goal that no longer matters.
note: Abandon suggests giving something up, often completely.

ru: стремящийся стать кем-либо; начинающий, подающий надежды
definition: Hoping and working to become successful in a particular profession or activity.
examples: The course is designed for aspiring lawyers.
She offers advice to aspiring entrepreneurs.
note: Attributive adjective: aspiring actor, writer, athlete. Distinguish from inspiring.

definition: To evaluate something again, especially because circumstances have changed.
examples: It may be time to reassess your career priorities.
The team reassessed the risks after receiving new evidence.
note: Reassess a situation, decision, priorities or risks.

definition: The quality of continuing to try despite difficulty, delay or opposition.
examples: Her persistence eventually led to success.
Persistence matters more than initial enthusiasm.
note: Often focuses on continuing a course of action; compare perseverance and determination.

definition: Highly skilled or successful in a particular activity or profession.
examples: She is an accomplished lawyer and negotiator.
He became an accomplished pianist through years of practice.
note: An accomplished professional has demonstrated skill or achievement; not simply finished.

definition: To build a stable professional position and reputation over time.
examples: She moved to London to establish a career in law.
It takes time to establish a career in a competitive field.
note: Often establish a career in a field; distinct from starting a first job.

definition: Continued effort and commitment despite setbacks, hardship or discouragement.
examples: Learning a language to an advanced level requires perseverance.
His perseverance helped him recover from several failures.
note: Often emphasizes endurance through hardship; compare persistence.

definition: A firm intention and strong resolve to achieve something.
examples: She showed remarkable determination throughout the project.
Talent alone is rarely enough without determination.
note: Determination highlights resolve; perseverance highlights continuing despite adversity.

definition: To actively work towards an objective that is difficult and demanding.
examples: He chose to pursue an ambitious goal in his career.
Pursuing an ambitious goal can require years of focused effort.
note: Pursue a goal, dream or ambition; not necessarily achieve it.

definition: Used to acknowledge a point that may weaken or qualify your argument.
examples: Admittedly, the plan is expensive, but it could work.
Admittedly, I underestimated how difficult it would be.
note: Sentence adverb for conceding a point before giving further context.

term: this is not to say that…
definition: Used to clarify that a statement should not be understood as making a broader claim.
examples: This is not to say that money is unimportant.
I value ambition. This is not to say that everyone must pursue the same goals.
note: Formal discourse marker used to prevent an overgeneralisation.

ru: тем не менее; при этом; вместе с тем
definition: Used to introduce a contrasting point or qualification to what was just mentioned.
examples: The job offers a good salary. That said, the hours are demanding.
It was a difficult year. That said, we made real progress.
note: Sentence connector, often at the start of a sentence; similar to nevertheless.

definition: Used to acknowledge a point before presenting a different perspective.
examples: Although this may be true, the long-term effects are uncertain.
Although this may be true, it does not justify the decision.
note: Concessive clause; the following main clause contrasts with the concession.

term: to sacrifice something on the altar of something
ipa: /tə ˈsækrɪfaɪs ˌsʌmθɪŋ ɒn ði ˈɔːltər əv ˌsʌmθɪŋ/
definition: To give up something valuable in order to prioritise another aim, belief or value.
examples: He sacrificed his health on the altar of career success.
We should not sacrifice fairness on the altar of efficiency.
note: Figurative, rhetorical expression; often critical of excessive priorities.

ru: за счёт чего-либо; в ущерб чему-либо
definition: In a way that harms or reduces one thing while benefiting another.
examples: He advanced his career at the expense of his health.
Speed should not come at the expense of accuracy.
note: Common: at the expense of quality, wellbeing, fairness; expense is singular here.

term: perseverance in the face of adversity
definition: Continued effort and resilience despite serious obstacles or hardship.
examples: Her perseverance in the face of adversity inspired the team.
The story celebrates perseverance in the face of adversity.
note: Relatively formal collocation for resilience amid hardship.

definition: To demonstrate the ability to keep trying when things are difficult.
examples: He showed perseverance after several failed attempts.
You need to show perseverance when learning a difficult skill.
note: Also demonstrate perseverance; often used in educational and motivational contexts.

ru: исключительное упорство; упорство само по себе
definition: Very great determination to keep trying, often presented as the main reason for success.
examples: She succeeded through sheer persistence.
His progress was the result of sheer persistence rather than luck.
note: Sheer intensifies the quality and suggests little else was needed.

definition: The habit of continuing a particular activity despite obstacles or repeated difficulty.
examples: Her persistence in applying for jobs eventually paid off.
Persistence in practising every day helped him improve.
note: Grammar: persistence in + -ing form; persistence in pursuing a goal.

definition: During the course of a journey, process or longer experience.
examples: I made several good friends along the way.
He encountered unexpected difficulties along the way.
note: Can describe a literal journey or progress towards a goal.

definition: To succeed in dealing with serious difficulties or hardship.
examples: She overcame adversity to build a successful career.
The team showed that it could overcome adversity.
note: Adversity is usually uncountable and more serious than an ordinary inconvenience.

definition: To produce a worthwhile result or reward after effort, time or investment.
examples: All those years of hard work finally paid off.
Her patience and persistence paid off in the end.
note: Here: an effort or investment pays off. Separate sense: pay off a debt means repay it.

definition: Extremely beautiful, interesting or enjoyable in a way that completely holds someone's attention.
examples: She has an entrancing voice that captivates everyone who hears her sing.
The film's entrancing atmosphere made it impossible to look away.
note: Often used with voice, music, beauty, atmosphere or performance; stronger and more evocative than interesting.

definition: Very loyal and committed to a person, belief or cause, especially when facing opposition or difficulties.
examples: She has always been a staunch supporter of human rights.
He remained a staunch critic of the government's proposed reforms.
note: Common: a staunch supporter, staunch defender, staunch advocate, staunch critic, staunch opposition. Emphasises firm, unwavering conviction.

ru: сделать вывод; прийти к заключению на основании имеющихся фактов
definition: To reach a conclusion based on available evidence, observations or reasoning rather than on an explicit statement.
examples: We can draw an inference from the available evidence that the decision was politically motivated.
It would be premature to draw any inferences from these preliminary findings.
note: Draw an inference (singular); draw inferences (plural). Common: draw an inference from the evidence, draw a reasonable inference, draw an adverse inference.

ru: приносить облегчение; ослаблять боль, стресс, тревогу или страдания
definition: To make someone feel less pain, worry or distress, or to improve a difficult situation.
examples: The medication brought immediate relief from the pain.
The news that she had recovered brought enormous relief to her family.
note: Common: bring relief to someone; bring relief from pain or stress; bring much-needed relief. Relief is uncountable in this sense (not 'a relief' in the phrase 'bring relief').

ru: ухитриться, умудриться; искусственно создать или подстроить; придумать хитроумный способ
definition: To manage to do something difficult or unexpected, often by using clever methods, or to arrange something deliberately and sometimes artificially.
examples: He contrived to finish the project despite having almost no resources.
The company contrived a reason to dismiss the employee.
note: Contrive to do something = manage to do it, sometimes improbably or ironically. Contrive something = invent or arrange it, often artificially. Contrived (adjective) = forced or unnatural.

definition: The formation or discharge of pus in an infected or inflamed part of the body.
examples: The doctor noticed signs of suppuration around the wound.
Persistent suppuration may indicate an underlying infection.
note: Formal medical term; everyday alternatives: pus formation or a wound producing pus. Related: suppurate (verb), suppurative (adjective).

definition: Having a dirty, patchy or unhealthy-looking coat of fur, or looking shabby and neglected.
examples: A mangy stray dog was wandering around the abandoned building.
He was wearing a mangy old coat that looked as though it hadn't been washed in years.
note: Originally related to mange, a skin disease in animals. Figuratively shabby or neglected; can sound disparaging when applied to people.
